$note: The same closing, with one attribute changed: the borrower asks to sign remotely.
Nothing in schedule.py knows anything about remote online notarization. It asks
the RON pack the same question it always asks, for every candidate day in the
horizon, and gets the same answer every time: not compliant. So the signing table
is empty, there is no feasible plan, and the receipt says why — California's
Online Notarization Act is signed law that is not yet operative (the pack encodes
its statutory outside date of 2030-01-01 and fails closed until then).
This is the point of the example stated in the negative. A scheduler that had a
state RON table hard-coded would either be wrong about California or would have to
be maintained in step with fifty legislatures. This one is neither, because it
